builder_plan.scenario: Your inference service slows down when several customers send requests together.
builder_plan.change: Replay a recorded request trace with only the proposed serving policy changed.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current scheduler on the same model and hardware.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Requests meeting your latency target, throughput, failures, and cost per successful request.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Governing Enterprise AI Traffic at Scale: Design and Operation of a Policy-Driven, Multi-Vendor LLM Gateway on Envoy
summary: Replaces direct per-vendor LLM API integration — with its credential sprawl, format lock-in, and ad hoc governance — with a centralized gateway that brokers credentials, normalizes API dialects, enforces declarative OPA policy, meters tokens, and manages budgets. Costs include operating and securing an always-on gateway tier (Envoy plus an external-processing service and WASM filter), the added latency on the request path, and the engineering burden of a policy control plane with approvals, pilots, and shadow rollouts. After adoption, the gateway becomes a single point of failure and policy bottleneck: misconfigured budgets or DLP rules can block or leak traffic, vendor API drift can break translation filters, and the enterprise scale (12,000 developers, 100+ models) has no counterpart on a small team's infrastructure.
rationale: The technique addresses multi-vendor governance at enterprise scale, while a small team on a constrained budget is better served by lightweight existing gateways or SDK-level routing rather than operating this architecture.
technique: Policy-driven multi-vendor LLM gateway on Envoy
